name: Badge
summary: Labels a status, count, or category.
description: A small pill-shaped label for short status, counts, or categories. It comes in four tones (default / secondary / destructive / outline), takes an optional leading icon, and binds its color, spacing, and full-radius shape to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Call out a status, state, or category — "Active", "Beta", "3 new"
Attach a short, at-a-glance label to another element
whenNotToUse: Triggering an action — use a Button
A removable or selectable token in an input — use a Chip

variant.default: Solid brand fill — highest emphasis, for the primary status.
variant.destructive: Solid danger fill — errors, blocked, or critical states.
variant.outline: Bordered with a transparent fill — the quietest tone.

states.default: Static label — a Badge is presentational and has no interactive states.

dos: Keep the text to a word or two
Bind the color to a semantic tone that matches the meaning
Pair color with text or an icon so the meaning survives without color
donts: Don't rely on color alone to convey status
Don't put an interactive control inside a badge — use a Button or Chip
Don't write full sentences — a badge is a label, not a message

notes: Renders as inline text, so the label is read in reading order
Convey status with text or an icon, not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
A leading icon is decorative (aria-hidden) — the text carries the meaning
